reference.source: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics / relevant specialty textbook
clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant syndrome caused by germline loss-of-function variants in the FLCN gene, which encodes the tumour-suppressor protein folliculin
Cutaneous hallmark is multiple fibrofolliculomas, small dome-shaped facial and upper-trunk papules, often with trichodiscomas and acrochordon-like lesions
Multiple basal, thin-walled pulmonary cysts predominate in the lung bases and predispose to recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax
Renal tumours are frequently bilateral and multifocal, characteristically hybrid oncocytic/chromophobe tumours, chromophobe or oncocytoma, though clear-cell types also occur
A spontaneous pneumothorax in a young adult, or a family history of pneumothorax with skin lesions, should prompt consideration of the diagnosis
Folliculin interacts with the AMPK and mTOR signalling networks, linking the syndrome to disordered cellular energy sensing and growth
Lifelong renal surveillance with periodic cross-sectional imaging (MRI preferred to limit radiation) allows early detection of tumours
reference.pathophysiology: Birt-Hogg-Dube syndrome is caused by germline inactivating variants in FLCN, encoding folliculin, a tumour-suppressor protein that participates in the AMP-activated protein kinase and mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) signalling pathways and in regulation of cellular metabolism and lysosomal function. Loss of folliculin function, typically with a somatic second hit in renal tissue, dysregulates growth and energy-sensing pathways and underlies the development of benign skin tumours, lung cysts and renal neoplasms. The precise mechanism linking folliculin loss to cyst formation and pneumothorax remains incompletely understood but reflects altered cell-cell adhesion and mechanical vulnerability of alveolar tissue.
additionalDifferentials: Tuberous sclerosis complex with facial angiofibromas and renal lesions
Familial spontaneous pneumothorax without renal or skin features
Von Hippel-Lindau disease with renal cell carcinoma
Multiple sporadic acrochordons or sebaceous hyperplasia
additionalInvestigations: Germline molecular genetic testing of FLCN including deletion/duplication analysis
Skin biopsy to confirm fibrofolliculoma or trichodiscoma when the diagnosis is uncertain
High-resolution chest CT to characterise basal pulmonary cysts
Renal MRI or CT surveillance for multifocal renal tumours
Cross-sectional imaging to define renal tumour size and growth over time
Family history documentation and cascade testing of relatives
redFlags: Sudden breathlessness and pleuritic pain indicating spontaneous pneumothorax
Solid or enlarging renal mass on surveillance imaging
Recurrent pneumothoraces requiring definitive surgical management
Haematuria or flank pain suggesting a symptomatic renal tumour
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is generally good with surveillance, as renal tumours often behave less aggressively than sporadic renal cell carcinoma and are amenable to nephron-sparing surgery when detected early. Recurrent pneumothorax and the cumulative renal tumour risk are the main sources of long-term morbidity.
pitfalls: Treating recurrent pneumothorax without recognising the underlying syndrome and its renal risk
Assuming a single renal oncocytoma is sporadic and not screening for further multifocal or contralateral tumours
Mistaking fibrofolliculomas for acne or ordinary skin tags
Relying on repeated CT surveillance and accumulating avoidable radiation when MRI is available
references: Emery and Rimoin's Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics
management: Lifelong renal surveillance with cross-sectional imaging, preferably MRI, to detect bilateral multifocal renal tumours at a treatable stage
Nephron-sparing surgery for renal tumours, reflecting their generally less aggressive behaviour than sporadic renal cell carcinoma
Anticipate and manage recurrent spontaneous pneumothorax, considering pleurodesis for recurrence and counselling on activities that raise risk
Cosmetic treatment of fibrofolliculomas and trichodiscomas by laser ablation or excision where desired
Establish the diagnosis by germline FLCN testing including deletion/duplication analysis
Provide genetic counselling and cascade testing of relatives, coordinating follow-up across genetics, urology and respiratory medicine
